messages.subject: what to use instead of 2-axes
parts:
Hi,

I have some data regarding performance prediction that I want to visualize. The data set consists of the measured throughput (y) against a number of threads (x-values), for different experiments. Additionally, I have the data obtained through different models (predicted throughput for the same number of threads as in the actual throughput). For each model, I calculated the error (from the actual data).

Now, I would like to present this data, so that I have the errors and the actual data on the same graph. So far, I had gnuplot scripts that would draw me a bunch of figures (one per experiment), where one axis is for the actual throughput, the other one for errors per model.

Since ggplot2 doesn't have support for 2-axes, do you have any suggestions how to visualize this data set? I would like to have both the actual throughput and the errors, not necessarily on the same graph.

I tried using facet_wrap, but there I can't have two panels, like here:
<http://rwiki.sciviews.org/doku.php?id=tips:graphics-ggplot2:aligntwoplots>


Thanks,
Nikola


An example of the data set would be:
exp<-c('geno','tera','stamp','x86')
thr<-c(1,16,32,48,64)
maxval<-sample(120:200,4)
vals<-rep(maxval,each=5)
vals<-vals*(1/thr)*rnorm(5,mean=1,sd=0.05)
data<-data.frame(exp=rep(exp,each=5),thr.num=rep(thr,times=4),perf=vals,mod1=rnorm(20),mod2=rnorm(20),mod3=rexp(20))
